verdicts.reason: Both fragments are literally in the source (H1 heading text and the adjoining info-macro paragraph) and are joined with an explicit '...' ellipsis, which is honest about the splice. The quote is genuinely in the source, but the statement over-reads it. Source: 'the category (e.g. plants for planting or cut wood), genus, species (for plants for planting)'. Grammatically the trailing parenthetical '(for plants for planting)' most naturally scopes only the immediately preceding item, 'species' — not 'genus' as well. This reading is reinforced elsewhere on the same page: the wood-caveats section names genera directly for non-planting wood products ('Wood, of Fraxinus, Castanea, Juglans, Pterocarya and Platanus...'), showing genus is asked about outside the plants-for-planting case too. The extract's statement ('the genus and species for plants for planting') silently resolves this ambiguity in favour of scoping both fields, and does so at 'verbatim' confidence, which overstates certainty — this is an inference, and a contestable one. See missed claim conf-005-m1 for the more defensible reading, and conf-005-m2 for the ambiguity itself as a gap.
